units.text: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 今天（10 月 6 日）发布博文，报道称苹果公司本月（2026 年 10 月）有望分 2 波推出诸多新产品，第一波聚焦智能家居产品，第二波主角是 Mac 系列，预估为 10 月最后 1 周。
IT之家此前援引彭博社马克 · 古尔曼（Mark Gurman）报道，苹果公司有望于 10 月 13 日发布其首款智能家居中枢（Home Hub）、Apple TV 4K（第四代）等产品。
而最新消息称苹果公司可能会在 10 月最后一周（26 日周一到 31 日周六），发布另一批新产品，预估聚焦 Mac 系列产品。
在产品方面，其主角是苹果首款触控 MacBook，现有爆料信息称该产品上市后名为“MacBook Ultra”，采用 OLED 显示屏，并采用更轻薄的机身设计。
苹果还可能发布搭载 M6 芯片的入门款 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，以及搭载 M6 芯片的新款 iMac。
苹果此前已宣布，搭载 M5 Ultra 芯片、配备 512GB 内存的高端 Mac Studio 配置将于 10 月下旬上市。该产品可能与 10 月最后一周的 Mac 新品发布安排重叠。
新款 iPad mini 也预计在 10 月亮相。相关信息显示，该产品可能配备 OLED 显示屏、A20 Pro 芯片、横向前置摄像头和重新设计的扬声器系统。

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple's $634 million patent loss to medical technology company Masimo has just gotten even bigger, after a federal judge ordered Apple to pay an additional $184 million in interest on what it owes (via Bloomberg Law ). The ruling takes Apple's bill to around $818 million, but that doesn't include any post-judgment interest continuing to accrue until the judgment is paid. Judge James Selna rejected Apple's argument that adding prejudgment interest would constitute a windfall for Masimo, citing U.S. Supreme Court guidance that "interest from the time that the royalty payments would have been received merely serves to make the patent owner whole." Put another way, Masimo is being compensated for as long as it was deprived of royalty payments that it theoretically would have received during the infringement period. It didn't all go Masimo's way, though. Selna also declined Masimo's request to calculate it at a 7 percent rate, which would have put Apple's interest bill at $243 million. Instead, the court used Masimo's own borrowing rate, compounding annually from when the infringement began. Masimo is also behind the separate patent dispute that led to a U.S. import ban on certain Apple Watch models and resulted in Apple disabling blood oxygen functionality on affected newly sold models. Apple in 2025 introduced a redesigned version of the feature. The dispute here is concerned with a Masimo pulse-oximetry patent. In November 2025, a jury found that Apple Watch features including heart-rate notifications infringed Masimo's patent and awarded the company $634 million. Apple subsequently tried to overturn or reduce the award, but Selna upheld the verdict in July. The patent in question expired in June 2022, so the ruling related to historical Apple Watch sales and has no effect on the heart-rate features in current Apple Watch models. Apple's $634 million patent loss to medical technology company Masimo has just gotten even bigger, after a federal judge ordered Apple to pay an additional $184 million in interest on what it owes (via Bloomberg Law).
The ruling takes Apple's bill to around $818 million, but that doesn't include any post-judgment interest continuing to accrue until the judgment is paid.

Judge James Selna rejected Apple's argument that adding prejudgment interest would constitute a windfall for Masimo, citing U.S. Supreme Court guidance that "interest from the time that the royalty payments would have been received merely serves to make the patent owner whole." Put another way, Masimo is being compensated for as long as it was deprived of royalty payments that it theoretically would have received during the infringement period.

It didn't all go Masimo's way, though. Selna also declined Masimo's request to calculate it at a 7 percent rate, which would have put Apple's interest bill at $243 million. Instead, the court used Masimo's own borrowing rate, compounding annually from when the infringement began.

Masimo is also behind the separate patent dispute that led to a U.S. import ban on certain Apple Watch models and resulted in Apple disabling blood oxygen functionality on affected newly sold models. Apple in 2025 introduced a redesigned version of the feature.

The dispute here is concerned with a Masimo pulse-oximetry patent. In November 2025, a jury found that Apple Watch features including heart-rate notifications infringed Masimo's patent and awarded the company $634 million.

Apple subsequently tried to overturn or reduce the award, but Selna upheld the verdict in July. The patent in question expired in June 2022, so the ruling related to historical Apple Watch sales and has no effect on the heart-rate features in current Apple Watch models.

units.text: Bloomberg reports that Apple’s plans for smart home products include devices, sensors, and cameras codeveloped in partnership with LG. Here are the details.
Apple and LG working together on domestic connected devices

According to Bloomberg, Apple and LG have been working together to develop a series of connected home products that will complement Apple’s upcoming smart home hub, marking “a formal reboot of HomeKit.”
That includes “a doorbell, thermostat, […] a smart deadbolt lock, indoor security camera, outdoor security camera and floodlight camera,” says Bloomberg.

Gurman notes that although Apple and LG “worked together to develop the accessories, the products will carry the LG brand,” adding that “the South Korean firm is handling manufacturing and product support” and has sought regulatory approval in recent weeks.

This arrangement with so-called second-party suppliers gives Apple a way to quickly expand its ecosystem without shouldering the full cost and complexity of producing and supporting a wide range of accessories. Apple can also help shape the products’ design, tailor their features and oversee engineering while keeping the work largely under wraps.

It is worth noting that although these products are part of Apple’s broader push into the connected home, which is expected to expand next week with the introduction of its new smart home hub, an updated Apple TV, and a new HomePod mini, Bloomberg says that “the products aren’t expected to reach consumers for at least a few more months.”
Here’s Bloomberg:

In recent weeks, LG has sought regulatory approval for the devices, including with the US Federal Communications Commission and UL Solutions, a product certification company. In many cases, the databases for both organizations include filings that reveal product names, specifications, features and drawings of the accessories.

That includes products labeled as the LG Video Doorbell Wired, LG Floodlight Cam, LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In, LG Indoor Cam Plug-In, LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG Smart Thermostat and LG Temperature Sensor. LG requested that photos and more precise details on the products remain confidential until early next year. The filings don’t mention Apple’s involvement.

When it comes to connectivity and standards, the report notes that many devices will support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread, and Matter. It adds that the smart lock also includes UWB (ultra-wideband), which will enable proximity-based features such as automatic door unlocking.
Finally, the report notes that for both Apple and LG, these products will mark a broader expansion into the smart home market, with Apple looking to give new momentum to its home ecosystem:

[Apple] is also planning its own additional offerings in the future, including a privacy-centric home-monitoring device, a version of its smart home hub that attaches the screen to a robotic arm, and an in-home security monitoring service, Bloomberg News has reported.

It is worth stressing that although today’s report comes on the heels of Apple’s announcement of the long-rumored ‘HomePad’ connected home hub and other products next week, the LG-made accessories aren’t expected to reach consumers for at least a few more months.
To read Bloomberg’s full report, follow this link.

units.text: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，华为海外 X 账号今日（10 月 6 日）发布了 9 月 29 日的国际媒体圆桌会议摘要。华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东与多家国际媒体的记者就华为消费者业务及 HarmonyOS 生态系统进行了交流。
有记者询问华为 Mate XT 2 三折叠手机的具体销售或出货量数据。此外，苹果也首次推出了其折叠形态产品，记者询问余承东如何看待这对华为在折叠屏手机行业地位的影响。
余承东回答称，Mate XT 2 是华为三折叠手机产品的第二代。第一代及其改款型号的销量超过 100 万部。第二代于 9 月 7 日上市。截至 9 月 29 日，Mate XT 2 已出货近 10 万台，预计总出货量也将超过 100 万部。
余承东表示，会逐步将 Mate XT 2 推向海外市场。“许多中东和亚太地区的用户都很喜欢它。我也希望能把它带到欧洲等其他市场。”
谈到苹果入局折叠屏手机市场，余承东表示很高兴看到美国同行最近推出了折叠屏手机。“实际上，华为在去年春天推出了一款类似的横向折叠产品 Pura X。当时，华为设计了这款折叠屏手机的小屏和大屏版本，最初计划同时发布。但由于投入了大量资源和精力建设 HarmonyOS 生态系统，华为将更大版本 Pura X Max 的发布推迟到了今年 4 月。”
余承东表示：“当我们准备推出这款阔折叠手机时，看到网上报道说我们的美国同行也开发了类似的手机。这款阔折叠手机最初来自华为，我们是更早开始做的。”
余承东还透露：“在 iPhone Duo 发布后的一周内，我们的 Pura X Max 销量增长了 76%。也许是因为消费者更喜欢我们的产品。自发布以来的几个月内，Pura X Max 的销量已突破 100 万台。我们欢迎同行加入竞争，为消费者提供更好的产品和服务。这种良性竞争也能激励更多用户选择折叠屏手机。”
余承东还表示，华为如今已占据中国折叠屏手机市场 75% 的份额。

余承东回答称，Mate XT 2 是华为三折叠手机产品的第二代。第一代及其改款型号的销量超过 100 万部。第二代于 9 月 7 日上市。截至 9 月 29 日，Mate XT 2 已出货近 10 万台，预计总出货量也将超过 100 万部。
余承东表示，会逐步将 Mate XT 2 推向海外市场。“许多中东和亚太地区的用户都很喜欢它。我也希望能把它带到欧洲等其他市场。”
谈到苹果入局折叠屏手机市场，余承东表示很高兴看到美国同行最近推出了折叠屏手机。“实际上，华为在去年春天推出了一款类似的横向折叠产品 Pura X。当时，华为设计了这款折叠屏手机的小屏和大屏版本，最初计划同时发布。但由于投入了大量资源和精力建设 HarmonyOS 生态系统，华为将更大版本 Pura X Max 的发布推迟到了今年 4 月。”
余承东还透露：“在 iPhone Duo 发布后的一周内，我们的 Pura X Max 销量增长了 76%。也许是因为消费者更喜欢我们的产品。自发布以来的几个月内，Pura X Max 的销量已突破 100 万台。我们欢迎同行加入竞争，为消费者提供更好的产品和服务。这种良性竞争也能激励更多用户选择折叠屏手机。”

The latest macOS 27.2 beta released this week further hints at the long-rumored MacBook with a touchscreen, which is expected to be unveiled by next month.

Specifically, when you click and hold on an app icon in the Dock on the third developer beta of macOS 27.2, the icon gets a little bit larger. A similar animation occurs when you long press on an iOS or iPadOS app, so the fact that the animation now extends to macOS could be another subtle clue that a touch-enabled MacBook is coming.
The new animation can be seen in videos shared by @madeby_ldt and @craigapplecom.

In particular, Apple reportedly plans to release new higher-end, higher-priced 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro or "MacBook Ultra" models with touchscreens in October or November.

In addition to a touch-enabled OLED display, these Macs are expected to feature M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, a thinner-and-lighter design, a Dynamic Island, and potentially Apple's C1X or C2 modem for built-in cellular connectivity.

units.text: iPhone Duo was officially unveiled in early September, but we continue to learn more about the device in the lead-up to its October launch. The latest reveal is a preview of the two-page PDF viewing experience on iPhone Duo.
Leak reveals expanded PDF feature set for iPhone Duo
If you’re interested in the iPhone Duo, there’s a good chance you want it to do things that your current iPhone can’t.
For example, lots of people interact with PDFs regularly as part of their job or for school. And viewing PDFs on a traditional iPhone isn’t a great experience.
iPads, by contrast, excel as PDF viewers. So how will the iPhone Duo fare?
Leaker pdfu has posted a video showing what iPhone Duo’s Quick Look feature for PDFs looks like in a new two-page mode.
Quick Look on iPhone Duo has a new two-page layout in the open book position. pic.twitter.com/gZtSH49rp1
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 6, 2026
The two-page layout could prove valuable in many cases. But I expect iPhone Duo will be especially nice for viewing PDFs in a single-page mode too.
Especially once Apple Pencil support launches later this year, iPhone Duo could be the first iPhone to offer a truly compelling PDF experience.
Do you plan to use iPhone Duo as a PDF viewer very often? What other tasks do you hope it can be great at that your current iPhone isn’t? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: The current beta of iOS 27.2 includes a Siri AI “suggested actions” feature in the Messages app that some will consider useful and others find annoying.
A developer who has found a number of unannounced features has discovered that Apple is seeking to keep everyone happy with a new set of options …
Suggested Actions in Messages

Suggested Actions were present in the initial iOS 27 beta, but Apple later pulled the feature after complaints that some of the suggestions were rather random. It subsequently returned in the beta of iOS 27.2. Here’s how Apple describes it:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

In the first example shown above, a group message chat contains a request for some shopping and to bring something left behind. The Messages app offers one-tap options to Add to Reminders and Add to Notes. In the second example, someone asks for specific photos to be shared, and the Messages app offers a button which leads directly to a search for matching photos.
Two ways to hide unwanted suggestions
Leaker pdfu found new controls in iOS 27.2 beta 3 to selectively toggle off unwanted suggestions.
Apple is working on granular controls for Suggested Actions in Messages, based on iOS 27.2 beta 3 code. pic.twitter.com/Fbffdf7epy
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 5, 2026

These allow suggestions to be toggled off by category, or you can let Siri AI monitor which ones you do and don’t use, and have it automatically hide the categories you haven’t used in the last 30 days.
These options aren’t yet live in the beta, but we can likely expect to see them soon.
9to5Mac’s Take
I’m certainly one of those who found many of them more annoying than useful, while I know others who are big fans, so this change ought to keep everyone happy.

units.text: Yet more code within the iOS 27 developer beta about Apple's plans for the home have included details of how HomePod mini surround sound will work with the rest of the ecosystem.

In retrospect the only unusual thing is that it took Apple years to figure out a way to make people buy four HomePod mini devices at a time. Then back in September 2026, it was revealed that Apple was working on how to join them together to make one home surround sound system.
Now prolific code sleuth pdfu has discovered further confirmation of the idea with details about Siri AI and home theater setups. Specifically, they've found that:
Siri can identify that a speaker belongs to a surround system
HomePods in a Home Theater group can pass Siri requests to Apple TV 4K
New HomePod light animation will play while using Siri AI

Those first two are about confirming whether the HomePod reacting to a request is part of a surround system. The code includes text saying "Accessory [X] is a speaker in surround system [Y]," for instance.
If the HomePod mini is in a system, then if there is also an Apple TV 4K in the setup, that speaker can relay requests to it.
The code at least implies that new Apple TV 4K will be needed. That's because what's described as a "separate, older path" retains the ability to send microphone audio to the Apple TV 4K device.
New HomePod light animation

It's the point about a new animation that is perhaps the clearest confirmation that Siri AI is indeed coming to HomePods. Leaker pdfu says it isn't clear when the new animation activates, but it's related to touch.
The animation is believed to be displayed when a user touches the HomePod, but Siri AI is currently processing a request.
So it's a touch rejection indicator. While pdfu has shown a demo of this, they say that the animations "are calculated by code in real time... [they] no longer use pre-computed frames."
Code leaker pdfu has a strong track record. They have previously revealed that the then-forthcoming iPhone Duo would use Touch ID, for instance.

units.text: IT之家 10 月 7 日消息，国外维修团队 iFixit 昨日（10 月 6 日）发布视频，拆解苹果 Apple Watch Series 12 与 Apple Watch Ultra 4 两款智能手表，最终打出 4/10 可维修得分。
报告显示，两款手表的屏幕均采用胶合固定，内部维修通常需要先拆下屏幕，IT之家附上拆解视频如下：
Apple Watch Ultra 4 配备 2.444 Wh 电池，高于 Ultra 3 的 2.313 Wh。更换电池仍需拆卸屏幕，机身底部的 4 颗螺丝只能打开后盖传感器组件，并接触机身上的 S11 芯片。
拆下屏幕后，Ultra 4 的电池与显示屏按压式连接器相对容易处理。但拆屏过程需要避开下方柔性排线，否则可能损坏内部连接结构。iFixit 最终给 Ultra 4 评出 4/10 分。
Apple Watch Series 12 采用 1.461 Wh 电池，高于 46 毫米 Series 11 的 1.403 Wh。苹果加入拉伸释放粘合剂和拉片，简化电池拆卸步骤。
Series 12 仍需先撬开胶合屏幕，才能进入内部。iFixit 拆解人员指出，该机屏幕周围的间隙比 Ultra 4 更紧，拆卸时需要更大力度，也增加屏幕受损风险。
苹果还将旧型号使用的 ZIF 连接器和胶带，替换为更简单的按压式连接器。由于更换屏幕时需要取出电池，屏幕维修与电池拆卸被绑定在同一流程中。

units.text: iPhone 18 Pro系列上市数周后，部分用户开始在社交平台反映酒红色机型的摄像头周围出现浅色或粉红色痕迹，黑色机型也有类似反馈。相关图片主要来自Reddit用户发帖，暂时没有证据显示这是普遍现象，也尚未确认痕迹究竟是表面褪色，还是油污、残留物等造成的视觉差异。
有用户称，摄像头镜圈附近的颜色比周围机身更浅，清洁后仍能看到差异；但其他用户认为部分图片呈现的可能只是指纹或皮脂，擦拭后会减轻。GSMArena表示，自己测试的酒红色iPhone 18 Pro Max暂未出现异常，不过测试机使用时间较少，也较少在户外使用。该媒体推测阳光中的紫外线可能与褪色有关，但目前没有实验或官方说明证实这一猜测。
这并非苹果Pro系列首次出现类似网络投诉。去年，部分iPhone 17 Pro和17 Pro Max用户也曾报告宇宙橙色机身以及深蓝色机身出现变色；当时同样没有明确证据证明影响范围或统一原因。苹果目前尚未公开确认iPhone 18 Pro存在涂层缺陷，也没有公布针对这批反馈的维修或更换方案。
苹果官网列出的iPhone 18 Pro系列配色包括黑色、银色、冰川色和全新酒红色，并称机身外壳采用铝材，其中85%为再生铝。现阶段褪色反馈集中在酒红色与黑色机型，但社交平台上的零散照片和用户描述不足以判断是否属于批次性质量问题，实际成因仍待苹果回应或更多案例核实。

units.text: Apple TV announced a new comedy series coming—The Choir—that reunites Ruth Jones and James Corden, the duo from beloved UK sitcom Gavin & Stacey.
The Choir is new Apple TV series from Ruth Jones and James Corden, reuniting the ‘Gavin & Stacey’ duo
Last year reporting indicated that Apple had struck a deal with Ruth Jones and James Corden for a new comedy series.
Now Apple has made it official: Jones and Corden are reuniting for The Choir, a new Apple TV series coming in 2027.

The duo might not be as well known to US viewers (though Corden has an established US track record), but they starred together in the massively popular UK sitcom Gavin & Stacey. For context, its series finale in 2024 became the UK’s most watched scripted show ever.
Here’s the official series summary for The Choir:

Brother and sister Ben (Corden) and Lisa (Jones) haven’t seen each other for several years. Ben has been living abroad, while Lisa has carried on in their small English town, where nothing ever happens. But when events take a sorry turn, Ben is forced to return to a life he never wanted, a town he never liked and a family from which he’s estranged. Can the unlikely healing of a rift with his big sister come in the form of a struggling local choir and the ensemble who sing their hearts out each week?
Guest stars include Hannah Waddingham, James McAvoy, and Jim Broadbent, and there’s a strong supporting cast too.
Apple describes the show as being a comedic drama about “family, friendship, love and music,” with a seemingly similar heartwarming feel to that of Gavin & Stacey.
Are you a fan of Gavin & Stacey? Is The Choir of interest to you? Let us know in the comments.
Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month, or you can get it discounted through the Apple One bundle.

units.text: Apple has released the second iOS 27.2 public beta, which includes the all-new Health app on iPhone.
iOS 27.2 beta includes all-new Health app and more
iOS 27.2 is the next release that will follow the official launch of iOS 27 from September 14. iOS 27.1 is just for iPhone Duo.
The first iOS 27.2 public beta included these changes:
Apple’s redesigned Health app first announced during the iPhone 18 Pro event is now live in this beta.
Dual capture mode comes to Group FaceTime.
Siri AI language support now includes French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
Apple TV app profiles come to iPhone.
Up Next is now New Episodes in Apple Podcasts. Continue Playing section is now directly below New Episodes. Podcasts also have color-matched backgrounds on episode lists.
Apple Music uses less of the icon’s color for labels in the app now.
iOS 27.2 is set to be released officially later this month. For now, there’s both a developer beta and public beta path for iPhone users looking to test the new Apple Health app early.

units.text: 苹果最新发布的macOS 27.2 Beta 3测试版本再次引发外界对触摸屏MacBook的猜测。开发者在系统代码中发现，苹果正在为多个系统应用加入新的触控手势支持，这被认为是苹果为未来触摸屏MacBook产品做准备的重要信号。
根据测试版本中的代码信息，备忘录应用新增了一项名为“ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer”的触控识别功能，快速预览（Quick Look）则加入了“dragTouch”能力。与此同时，Safari浏览器也增加了新的触控识别机制。不过，这些功能目前仅存在于系统底层代码中，尚未正式向用户开放。
事实上，关于苹果开发触摸屏MacBook的传闻已经持续多年。虽然苹果历史上长期坚持Mac和iPad采用不同交互方式，但近年来相关迹象越来越多，显示公司正在逐步强化macOS对触控操作的支持。
业内人士认为，这些新增功能可能同时服务于两个方向。一方面，它们能够进一步增强Sidecar功能。Sidecar允许用户将iPad作为Mac的扩展显示器使用，而最新版macOS已经开始支持通过iPad直接对Mac界面进行触控操作。另一方面，这些新增触控手势也可能是在为未来的触摸屏MacBook做准备。
分析指出，如果苹果正在开发触摸屏MacBook，那么为Safari、备忘录以及其他系统应用逐步加入原生触控支持将是必要步骤。通过提前在macOS层面完善触控交互体验，苹果能够确保相关硬件发布时拥有更加成熟的软件生态。
近年来，苹果已经开始在多个产品和系统之间共享底层技术成果。例如某项为iPad开发的功能最终可能被应用到Mac产品线，而Mac端的技术改进也可能反向推动其他平台的发展。此次在macOS 27.2中发现的新触控功能，被认为正体现了这种统一开发策略。
此前的macOS Golden Gate版本已经为Sidecar带来了更完整的触控支持，使用户能够通过iPad直接操作Mac界面。如今随着更多应用开始加入专门的触摸识别能力，外界普遍认为苹果正在进一步推进这一方向。
目前尚不清楚这些新手势最终会以怎样的形式呈现给用户，也无法确定它们究竟是为Sidecar升级准备，还是专门针对未来触摸屏MacBook开发。不过，多方爆料均指出，苹果首款配备触摸屏的MacBook Pro有望在2026年10月至11月期间正式发布。
如果相关传闻属实，那么即将到来的新款MacBook不仅将成为苹果历史上首款支持触控操作的Mac笔记本，还可能搭载OLED显示屏等多项重大升级。而最新的macOS 27.2开发进展，则进一步增强了外界对于这一产品即将问世的预期。

units.text: 苹果最新发布的macOS 27.2开发者测试版再次释放出触控MacBook即将到来的信号。多方迹象显示，苹果正在持续为首款支持触摸操作的Mac笔记本进行软件层面的准备，而这款备受关注的新产品最快有望在未来数周内正式亮相。
根据开发者在macOS 27.2 Beta 3中的发现，当用户在Dock栏中长按应用图标时，图标会出现放大动画效果。类似的交互方式早已存在于iPhone和iPad系统中，长按应用图标会触发相关操作菜单。如今这套动画被引入macOS，被认为是苹果正在为触摸输入体验做准备的又一项细微变化。
除了新的Dock动画之外，macOS 27.2还新增了多项与触控手势相关的系统代码。苹果在Safari、照片、备忘录以及Quick Look等应用中加入了新的手势识别组件，包括触摸识别器、长按识别功能以及拖拽触控支持等内容。这些改动表明，未来的macOS应用正在逐步获得更完善的触屏交互能力。
不过，外界也指出，这些新功能并不一定完全是为触控MacBook而设计。部分代码同样可能用于增强Sidecar功能。Sidecar允许用户使用iPad作为Mac的第二显示器，而macOS Golden Gate此前已经为该功能引入了完整的触摸输入支持。因此，苹果扩大触控手势覆盖范围，也有可能同时服务于Sidecar和未来的触屏Mac产品。
尽管如此，越来越多的软件迹象与供应链传闻正在相互印证。报道指出，苹果预计将在今年10月或11月推出全新的高端MacBook产品线，外界普遍认为其可能被命名为MacBook Ultra，或作为新一代MacBook Pro上市。这将成为苹果历史上首款原生支持触摸操作的Mac电脑。
除了触控功能之外，这款新机还预计将首次为MacBook产品配备OLED显示屏，并搭载M5 Pro和M5 Max处理器。与此同时，新产品据称将采用更加轻薄的机身设计，可能加入类似iPhone的Dynamic Island区域，并有望整合苹果自研蜂窝网络调制解调器，从而提供内置移动网络连接能力。
随着macOS不断加入更多面向触摸操作的特性，包括此前已经出现的下拉刷新功能以及如今不断扩展的手势支持，苹果多年未曾实现的“触屏Mac”构想似乎正逐步走向现实。如果相关传闻准确，那么苹果将在未来数周内开启Mac产品线的重要转变，为MacBook带来自诞生以来最重大的交互方式变革之一。

units.text: IT之家 10 月 7 日消息，据彭博社马克 · 古尔曼报道，苹果公司即将发力智能家居设备赛道，其中将包含门铃、恒温器以及其他配件，这批产品是通过与 LG 电子开展一次不同寻常的合作所开发的。
知情人士透露，这批产品将归入一套设备生态体系，可以适配苹果全新的智能家居中枢，同时也能够搭配升级后的 HomePod mini 以及新款电视机顶盒使用。苹果计划在 10 月 13 日正式发布这批全新设备。
因该合作项目尚未对外公开，相关消息人士要求匿名。据他们介绍，和 LG 电子联合开发的产品清单还包括智能插锁、室内安防摄像头、室外安防摄像头以及泛光灯摄像头。
尽管两家企业共同参与配件的研发工作，但成品将会打上 LG 的品牌，由这家韩国企业负责生产以及后续的产品技术支持。
苹果此前就采用过类似策略：该公司曾经低调和富士康科技集团旗下的贝尔金、罗技国际股份有限公司（Logitech International SA）等企业合作开发产品，最终由合作方自有品牌对外销售。
这种与所谓第二方供应商开展合作的模式，可以让苹果快速扩充自家设备生态，而不需要承担大批量配件生产与售后带来的高额成本以及复杂事务。苹果还可以参与把控产品设计、定制产品功能、监督工程开发，同时让大部分相关研发工作处于保密状态。
LG 这边的配件研发进度落后于苹果自研设备，这批产品预计至少还需要数月时间才能够面向消费者发售。
最近几周，LG 已经陆续为这批设备向监管机构提交认证申请，其中包括美国联邦通信委员会以及产品认证机构 UL Solutions。两家机构的数据库内已经存有申报材料，部分文件披露了这批配件的产品名称、规格参数、功能说明以及工程图纸。
申报清单里出现的产品包括 LG 有线视频门铃、LG 泛光灯摄像头、LG 可插电室外摄像头、LG 可插电室内摄像头、LG 智能插锁、LG 智能恒温器以及 LG 温度传感器。LG 申请将产品实拍照片以及更多精确细节保密至明年年初；这些申报文件当中并未提及苹果参与开发的相关信息。
多数设备同时支持无线网络与蓝牙，另外还兼容 Thread 与 Matter 协议，这两项是近几年苹果及其竞争对手都普遍采用的智能家居通信协议。这款门锁还支持超宽带技术（UWB），借助该功能，用户走到家门附近时门锁就可以自动解锁。
对于苹果而言，这套全新家居生态与相关设备，意味着 HomeKit 正式重启。苹果在 2014 年就推出了 HomeKit 平台，但和亚马逊以及 Alphabet 旗下谷歌的同类产品相比，该平台一直没能打开市场局面。
据报道，苹果希望依靠这批智能家居硬件以及 Siri 人工智能助手，重新激活智能家居业务。该公司后续还规划了更多自研产品：一款主打隐私保护的居家监控设备；屏幕搭载机械臂版本的智能家居中枢；还有一项居家安防监控服务。
LG 原本的核心产品是电视与洗衣机，这批设备也代表着其自身智能家居业务的扩张。这套产品线是该企业近十年来首次推出室内摄像头，同时也是其近期历史上首次推出室外摄像头、恒温器、泛光灯摄像头以及可视门铃；这款智能锁更是 LG 首次面向韩国以外市场发售的智能门锁产品。
此番合作之后，苹果与 LG 将会和已经牢牢占据智能家居市场的亚马逊 Ring 以及谷歌 Nest 形成更为直接的竞争。后两家厂商早已推出全套同类设备，方便用户监控住宅内部以及房屋周边区域的状况。
IT之家注意到，苹果与 LG 之间有着长期的合作渊源。二者曾经在智能手机领域互为竞争对手，如今 LG 电子的若干姊妹企业已经成为苹果至关重要的合作伙伴。LG 显示（LG Display）为苹果多款设备供应显示屏；苹果此前还和 LG 电子展开协作，把自家服务集成到 LG 的电视当中。
差不多十年之前，苹果一度暂时退出外接显示器市场，当时它就曾与 LG 联合开发显示器，适配这家手机厂商的笔记本电脑产品。

units.text: 微博爆料者“数码闲聊站”（Instant Digital）称，苹果曾计划为iPhone 18 Pro系列和折叠屏手机iPhone Duo配备16GB内存，但后来调整了方案。爆料没有说明苹果何时考虑过这一配置，也未交代改动原因，因此16GB只能视为未经苹果证实的早期规划传闻。
目前，iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max的内存容量已从Xcode 27开发工具数据中得到确认，均为12GB，与上一代Pro机型相同。iPhone Duo尚未出现在相关Xcode数据中；由于它与Pro系列搭载相同的A20 Pro芯片，外界预计内存也为12GB，但这一点还没有得到独立验证。苹果官网公布了两款设备搭载A20 Pro，却没有在产品规格中列出内存容量。
苹果于今年9月发布iPhone 18 Pro系列和iPhone Duo。官方称，两款Pro机型采用A20 Pro芯片，内存带宽比上一代A19 Pro提升50%；Duo则是苹果首款折叠屏iPhone，采用同款芯片，配备7.6英寸内屏和5.4英寸外屏，并支持Apple Intelligence与新一代Siri。苹果已公布Duo将于10月16日开启预订、10月23日上市。
Apple Intelligence功能对设备内存的需求不断提高。苹果支持页面显示，运行新一代Apple Intelligence的部分设备需至少配备12GB统一内存，并为设备端模型预留最高14GB存储空间；这说明内存是本地AI体验的重要硬件条件，但并不能证明苹果曾规划16GB就是为了某项特定功能。
内存供应紧张可能是苹果调整配置的背景之一。此前分析师郭明錤称，DRAM短缺正影响苹果2026年的硬件出货安排；有关折叠屏机型采用12GB内存的供应链报道也提到，内存价格上涨。不过，苹果和爆料者都没有证实供应短缺导致16GB方案被取消，具体原因仍不清楚。

units.text: Rumors have shown that Apple is working on various smart home accessories, and it seems that a doorbell, thermostat, and more will be developed with LG as a partner.

An unannounced Apple Home event is expected to take place on October 13 with a new Apple TV, upgraded HomePod mini, and the debut of the long-rumored Apple Home Hub. A new last-minute rumor suggests that additional home accessories could be coming soon to accompany Apple's new home initiatives.

According to a report from Bloomberg, Apple is working with LG to introduce a smart deadbolt lock, an indoor security camera, an outdoor security camera, and a floodlight camera. These will be branded as LG in spite of Apple's involvement, similar to how Apple has co-developed iPhone accessories with other companies previously.
For example, the LG UltraFine Display was co-developed between LG and Apple.
It isn't clear if these devices from LG are the same ones previously rumored to be coming from Apple. Rumors suggested Apple would make its own security camera, doorbell, and similar products.

LG's products are currently going through regulatory submissions, but those filings do not mention Apple. It could be early 2027 before LG is ready to launch these products, and it isn't clear when they will be revealed.
The Apple Home announcement is set for October 13. It is expected to reveal multiple products as an attempt to revitalize Apple's place in the smart home industry.

units.text: Apple has issued release candidates for macOS Sequoia 16.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, with the minor updates making the older operating systems more secure.

While Apple's main focus is on updating its 27-generation operating systems, it also periodically updates its previous releases. In one release to testers on October 6, Apple is preparing two such updates for macOS Tahoe and macOS Sequoia.

The release candidates of macOS 16.8.2 and macOS 26.7.2 mean Apple believes the updates are in a position where they can be released to the public. That could happen within days, unless a second RC round is needed.
The RC builds are:
macOS 16.8.2 RC 1 is build 24H219
macOS 26.7.2 RC 1 is build 25G320

As expected for these sorts of updates, Apple isn't including any new features. However, they will contain the typical mix of bug fixes, performance improvements, and security fixes that Apple usually recommends for all users.

AppleInsider and Apple strongly advise that users do not install test operating systems or other beta or RC software onto "mission-critical" or primary hardware. This is due to the small chance of issues that could result in the loss of data.
Testers should therefore use secondary or non-essential devices and make sure they have sufficient backups of any critical data.

units.text: 一台罕见的苹果一号电脑（Apple I）正在邦瀚斯拍卖行进行线上拍卖，开放竞价期为10月4日至14日，估价为50万至80万美元（约合人民币359万至539万元）。这台电脑被称为“哈特菲尔德”（Hatfield）苹果一号，由原主人弗雷德·哈特菲尔德于1976年购入。主板上留有苹果联合创始人史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克的亲笔签名，且至今仍处于可工作状态。
拍卖品中还附有一封1978年1月18日由史蒂夫·乔布斯亲笔签名的信件，信中乔布斯提出让哈特菲尔德支付400美元，交回这台苹果一号换购一台Apple II主板，但哈特菲尔德拒绝了这笔交易，也正是这个“拒绝”，让这台电脑得以完整保存至今。
据悉，苹果一号是苹果公司的首款产品，诞生于1976年。当时乔布斯和沃兹尼亚克说服电子产品零售商Byte Shop的老板保罗·特雷尔进货50台组装好的电路板，由此正式创办了苹果电脑公司。
苹果一号以裸板形式出售，不包含机箱、电源、键盘和显示器，搭载MOS 6502处理器，主频1MHz，标配4KB内存（可扩展至8KB或48KB），原始售价为666.66美元。
关于这个略带“魔鬼数字”意味的定价，一种说法是沃兹尼亚克喜欢重复数字，另一种说法是批发价500美元加上约三分之一利润后自然得出。
苹果一号总共生产了约200台，随着时间推移大量被丢弃或损毁，目前全球确认存世的不足75台。
近年来苹果一号在拍卖市场上屡创高价，2014年一台曾拍出90.5万美元，2025年3月另一台以37.5万美元成交。此次拍卖的“哈特菲尔德”版因兼具沃兹尼亚克签名、乔布斯亲笔信件和可工作状态，被拍卖行视为近年来品质最好的苹果一号之一。
从666美元到最高估价80万美元，50年间身价翻了约1200倍，堪称理财神器。拍卖前该电脑曾在洛杉矶、波士顿、旧金山和纽约进行公开展示。

units.text: With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value.

When it first launched, the M4 Mac mini provided a huge bang for the buck. Not only did it feature Apple’s M4 SoC, but it also came with a healthy 16GB of unified memory, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, two front-facing USB 3 ports, HDMI, and Ethernet. At just $599 or $499 at the student discount price, the M4 Mac mini was not only the most versatile Mac in Apple’s lineup but also, pound for pound, the best Mac in the lineup.
Video: Apple killed the Mac mini’s best hidden feature :(
Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

But Apple’s smallest Mac had a secret up its sleeve that made it an even more valuable machine: a slot for upgradable storage. Users could literally pry open the machine’s back cover, unscrew a few screws, and access a removable NAND module that could be easily replaced with a third-party SSD up to 2TB.

The benefits were multifaceted. Not only could you upgrade the SSD or easily fix a drive that failed, but you could also save some serious coin by forgoing Apple’s build-to-order upgrade option and do it yourself with a much cheaper third-party SSD.
Upgrading the M4 Mac mini SSD

At the time, Apple charged $800 for the 2TB upgrade, transforming the “budget” computer into a $1400 computer with the click of an option. By upgrading after purchase with a third-party SSD, users could save nearly $500.

Of course, as someone who likes to tinker, I was extremely excited about this and ended up posting a full video tutorial showing, step by step, how to upgrade the stock SSD with a third-party drive. It proved to be quite popular, amassing half a million views.
Video: How to upgrade the M4 Mac mini SSD
It was nice while it lasted.

With the launch of this latest generation of Mac mini, Apple has soldered the SSD directly to the logic board, effectively eliminating the ability to upgrade it post-purchase with a third-party NAND module.

The Mac mini has gone from what was hands-down the best bang-for-your-buck Mac to a significantly more expensive product, not just for the base model, which goes from $600 to $900, but also for the 2TB upgrade, which goes from $800 to $1000.

Today if you want an M6 Mac mini with a 2TB SSD, you’ll need to pay Apple $1900. The equivalent M4 Mac mini, with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade, would have set you back roughly $920 when you factor in the $320 aftermarket upgrade price being charged at the time. Obviously, things have gotten more expensive, so it’s not exactly Apple’s to Apple’s (see what I did there), but that’s a $1000 increase in price, not only because Apple is charging significantly more, but also because Apple eliminated the ability for customers to upgrade the machines themselves.

I have a good idea as to why Apple opted to increase the price of the base Mac mini by $300, and I can even understand why its SSD prices have increased so much. Because of AI and other factors, component, SSD, and memory prices have all skyrocketed. But that doesn’t explain why Apple opted to solder the SSDs to the logic board instead of keeping them user-replaceable like before.

We can speculate, but we may never know the real answer for Apple’s decision to revert back to soldered SSDs. What we do know, however, is that these machines are significantly more expensive, and even that sounds like an understatement. In the case of the M4 Mac mini with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade vs the M6 Mac mini with a 2TB build-to-order upgrade, it’s roughly a 106% price increase.
9to5Mac’s Take

It can be difficult to find a base model M4 Mac mini on the used market at a reasonable price, but if you can manage to do so, it remains an excellent machine for its baseline performance, features, and upgradable SSD.

The good news in all of this is that all of Apple’s Mac mini models come with Thunderbolt connectivity, so you can easily add high-bandwidth external storage via a USB or Thunderbolt SSD. I’m personally a big fan of the Samsung T9, which offers a relatively affordable way to add extra storage.
What do you think Apple’s reasoning is for getting rid of user-replaceable SSDs in the Mac mini? Do you have any particular theories? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts.

units.text: Apple is being ordered to pay an extra $184 million to Masimo as part of the Apple Watch blood oxygen sensor trial, as an interest payment on top of the existing $634 million fine.

In November 2025, Masimo was awarded $634 million in compensation, after a federal jury agreed heart rate notification features and the Apple Watch workout mode violated its patents. Eleven months later, Apple has to pay even more.
An October 5 ruling by Federal Judge James Selina rejected an argument from Apple that adding interest to the existing award would be a windfall for Masimo, reports Bloomberg Law.
The judge cited guidance from the U.S. Supreme Court that the interest from the time that royalty payments would have been normally received "merely serves to make the patent holder whole."
In short, it's not a windfall, it's what Masimo was due, and now Apple has to pay it. The interest brings the total payments from Apple to Masimo up to $818 million.
It's not entirely bad news for Apple. It could've paid a lot more.

The judge rejected Masimo's demand for an intrest rate of 7%, and instead decided that the payment would be based on Masimo's own borrowing rate, compounding. If Masimo had its way, Apple would be paying $243 million in interest, an increase of $59 million.
A lengthy legal saga
Apple's courtroom activity with Masimo started back in 2020, over accusations that the Apple Watch infringed 10 patents and Apple's alleged stealing of trade secrets through hiring ikey personnel.
More lawsuits were filed in 2021 by Masimo, declaring that the Apple Watch Series 6 should be banned from sale for five patent infringements over blood oxygen measuring technology.

Lawfare continued in 2023, leading up to Apple preparing to stop sales of the Apple Watch at the end of that year to comply with an ITC ruling. However, after a temporary stay on December 27, 2023, it was determined that stripping out blood oxygen sensing in code would be enough to get around the ban.
The change allowed Apple to restore the feature to devices sold in the U.S. during the ban period, 18 months later.

Masimo was given its $634 million verdict in November 2025, with jurors agreeing that heart rate notification features and the Apple Watch's workout mode violated patents. The royalty figure was at the lower end of Masimo's requested range, but far higher than Apple's estimate of $3 million to $6 million.

By April 2026, Masimo's complaint over the USITC's decision to deny a reinstatement of the Apple Watch ban was dismissed with prejudice by a U.S. District Court. Not long after, in July 2026, Apple's attempt to appeal against the $634 million award was rejected.

evidence.raw_lead: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman recently reported that Apple plans to unveil an all-new home hub, a new HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K on Tuesday, October 13, and MacRumors has since learned about another launch slated for later in the month. units.text: Sources: Apple Planning Two Sets of Product Launches in October

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman recently reported that Apple plans to unveil an all-new home hub, a new HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K on Tuesday, October 13, and MacRumors has since learned about another launch slated for later in the month.
Apple is planning to unveil additional new products in the final week of October, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.

While we do not know exactly which products Apple plans to announce in the final week of October, the most likely possibilities are all Macs, including the long-rumored "MacBook Ultra" models with OLED displays and a thinner-and-lighter design, a base model 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, and an iMac with an M6 chip.
Apple also previously announced that it will be releasing a high-end Mac Studio configuration with the M5 Ultra chip and 512GB of RAM in "late October."

Another new product expected this October is a new iPad mini with an OLED display, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape front camera, a redesigned speaker system, and more. It is unclear if the device will be announced alongside new home products on October 13, alongside new Macs in the final week of October, or at some other point this month.

All in all, it appears that Apple has two sets of product launches planned for this October, and that is on top of the iPhone Duo launching on Friday, October 23. Get ready, as it is about to be a busy couple of weeks in the world of Apple.

units.text: Apple executive chair and former CEO Tim Cook sold nearly 200,000 Apple shares on October 2, one day after more than 374,000 restricted stock units vested as part of his compensation package. Here are the details.
Cook still holds more than 3.2 million Apple shares
As reported by Investing.com (via MacMagazine), Tim Cook sold 191,753 Apple shares on October 2, following the settlement of 374,541 restricted stock units (RSUs) on October 1.

RSUs are a form of stock-based compensation that entitle an employee to receive company shares once certain conditions are met. In Cook’s case, the number of shares that vested was determined by Apple’s total shareholder return relative to other S&P 500 companies over a three-year period.

According to the filing, Cook’s shares were sold across multiple transactions at prices ranging from $330.66 to $334.50 per share. At the time of publication, Apple stock was trading at $333.84 per share.
The report adds:
Apple withheld 199,038 shares, valued at $65,746,232 based on a price of $330.32 per share, to cover tax withholding requirements related to the RSU vesting.

Investing.com notes that the sale was carried out under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan that Cook adopted in May, meaning the transaction had been arranged in advance rather than decided on the day of the sale.
Cook also transferred 26,325 Apple shares as a gift on October 2, although the filing does not identify the recipient.
Even after the sale, the tax withholding, and the gifted shares, Cook still holds more than 3.2 million Apple shares through his trust.
To read Investing.com’s full report, follow this link. For the original filing, follow this link.

evidence.discovery_lead: Yesterday we reported that Apple tripled the number of iCloud Mail aliases users can create, from three to nine . But it turns out that's not the only email-related limit Apple has raised. The company has also bumped the number of iCloud Custom Domains users can set up with iCloud+, from three to 10. If you subscribe to iCloud+, you can use a domain name you already own for your iCloud Mail address. So instead of name@icloud.com, your address can be anything@yourdomain.com. You can also buy a new domain when setting up the feature. The increased number of custom domains allowed was spotted in Apple's support documentation by X account pdfu . units.text: 苹果正在为Apple Music更换自2015年服务上线以来的首个Logo。最新发布的macOS 27.2开发者测试版显示，苹果对Apple Music的文字标识进行了重新设计，将原本的“Music”改为更加粗厚的字体，同时全部采用小写字母，整体视觉也因此变得更加醒目和宽大。
这一变化最早出现在macOS 27.2 Beta 3中，随后也在iOS 27.2 Beta 3中被发现。相关变化并不是简单调整字体大小，而是直接改变了Logo的字形风格。新的“music”采用明显更厚的字体，同时取消原来的首字母大写设计，使整个Logo呈现出更加厚重、现代的视觉效果。
由于字体重量增加，加上全部采用小写字母，新版Logo的整体宽度也有所增加。与Apple Music过去使用了11年的标识相比，新设计显得更加大胆，也更加接近近年来科技品牌普遍采用的粗体、简洁视觉风格。
目前Apple Music的主要Logo仍然保留着音乐符号与文字组合的设计语言，因此这次改版并不是彻底推翻原有品牌形象，而是在保留Apple Music辨识度的基础上，对文字部分进行现代化调整。
Apple Music于2015年正式推出，因此此次变化也是该服务上线11年来首次进行Logo层面的重大更新。相比苹果硬件产品和系统界面经常进行视觉调整，Apple Music的品牌标识此前一直保持相对稳定。
新版Logo实际上已经不只存在于测试系统中。在伦敦Apple Music Hall的宣传视频中，新旧两个版本的Logo已经同时出现。这表明苹果至少已经开始在部分线下宣传场景中使用新的品牌标识，而不只是把它作为系统测试中的实验设计。
从品牌定位来看，Apple Music本身也是苹果服务体系中相对年轻化的一项产品。与Apple TV、iCloud等更加偏向工具和服务属性的产品相比，音乐流媒体业务需要更加突出年轻、潮流和娱乐属性。因此，苹果选择通过更加粗厚、醒目的字体强化Apple Music的视觉识别度，并不令人意外。
目前苹果尚未正式宣布新版Apple Music Logo，也没有公布具体的全面推送时间。不过，既然新版Logo已经出现在macOS 27.2和iOS 27.2的测试版本中，同时又出现在Apple Music Hall的宣传材料里，其正式启用应该只是时间问题。
苹果预计将于10月13日举行一场特别活动，因此这可能成为新版Apple Music Logo正式亮相的一个时间节点。当然，目前并没有确切消息证明苹果一定会在这场活动中公布Logo变化。
如果最终正式启用，这次更新的意义更多体现在品牌视觉层面，而不是功能变化。Apple Music本身的音乐库、推荐系统以及其他核心功能不会因为Logo变化而发生改变。
不过，对于已经使用11年的品牌标识而言，即使只是字体和大小写形式的变化，也代表苹果希望让Apple Music的视觉形象与当前的苹果生态以及年轻用户群体更加匹配。新版粗体、小写“music”相比过去更加醒目，也可能更适合出现在音乐会、社交媒体以及大型宣传活动等场景中。
目前来看，Apple Music这次改版并没有采用完全激进的设计，而是采取了“保留品牌核心元素、重新调整文字风格”的方式。对于一个已经拥有庞大用户群的成熟服务而言，这种改动既能够带来新鲜感，又不会让用户完全失去原有的品牌认知。

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple is working with LG Electronics on smart home accessories that will integrate with the upcoming home hub and other Apple home products, reports Bloomberg . LG is making a wired video doorbell, thermostat, smart deadbolt lock, temperature sensor, indoor security camera, outdoor security camera, and floodlight camera, according to documents LG submitted to the Federal Communications Commission and UL Solutions. Apple is not mentioned in the filings, and LG asked the FCC to keep details confidential. The devices will be built and branded by LG, though Bloomberg says Apple helped develop them. This arrangement with so-called second-party suppliers gives Apple a way to quickly expand its ecosystem without shouldering the full cost and complexity of producing and supporting a wide range of accessories. Apple can also help shape the products' design, tailor their features and oversee engineering while keeping the work largely under wraps. While Apple is expected to introduce the rumored home hub, a new Apple TV 4K, and a new HomePod mini on October 13, the LG accessories won't be ready to launch for a few months. Several of LG's devices support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread, and Matter, with the lock also offering UWB support for close-proximity auto-unlocking. Apple has worked with LG frequently. It uses LG Display components in its devices, and when Apple didn't sell Apple-branded displays, it teamed up with LG for 4K and 5K UltraFine monitors made for Macs. LG is not known for smart home accessories, but it bought a majority stake in smart home platform Homey in 2024. LG may be aiming to compete with Samsung SmartThings, Amazon Ring, Google Nest, and other smart home brands. Tags: Apple Command Center , LG This article, " LG Making Doorbell, Lock, and Cameras for Apple's Home Hub " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

units.text: Three Years of 80% Charge Limits on iPhone: The Results

Since 2023, Apple's newer iPhones have had an 80 percent charge limit for those who want to extend battery lifespan. Charging to 80 percent instead of 100 percent is supposed to put less stress on the battery, improving longevity.
For the last three years, I've used that setting on my iPhone. I started with the iPhone 15 Pro Max, then did the iPhone 16 Pro Max, and most recently, the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
After 12 months at an 80 percent maximum charge, my iPhone 17 Pro Max is at 97 percent maximum capacity with a cycle count of 277.
Last year, my iPhone 16 Pro Max was at 94 percent capacity after 12 months, and in 2024, my iPhone 15 Pro Max was also at 94 percent capacity.

During the year I tested the ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max, I tried not to let the battery dip below 20 percent. This year, I did the same thing, but I also tried to do more charging over USB-C than Qi2 or MagSafe. I'm not sure if that helped, but 97 percent capacity is the best result I've had yet with the charge limit turned on.
I don't know how my battery result compares to others, but if you've kept yours at 100 percent, you can compare your capacity to mine to see if there's any real difference.

Apple transitioned to aluminum and added vapor chamber cooling with the ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max, and I did think my iPhone spent less time uncomfortably warm than the ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max. It may be that the vapor chamber cooling made the biggest difference and limiting wireless charging didn't matter.

I don't use the iPhone 15 Pro Max or the ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max as my main iPhones anymore, but I do use them daily as test devices. They still have the 80 percent limit turned on, so I can share some longer-term battery results.
iPhone 15 Pro Max (36 months) - 88%, 369 cycles
‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max (24 months) - 93%, 343 cycles
‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max (12 months) - 97%, 277 cycles

Last year, my ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max hit 299 cycles by September 24. This year, I'm only at 277 cycles. It's nearly two weeks later than I usually report results too, so the larger battery meant less charging.

The ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max has a bigger battery and faster charging than the ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max, so an 80 percent charge limit wasn't as difficult to live with as it was in the past. I rarely ran out of battery, though I did still bring a battery pack with me most places. My favorite battery packs right now are the ones with built-in USB-C cables, especially those that can attach to my iPhone magnetically but charge it over USB-C. It's faster charging that's still convenient. I also continue to be a fan of the super-slim battery packs that add little bulk and weight to an iPhone.

For the iPhone 15 Pro Max and ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max, I didn't think sacrificing a fifth of my battery was worth the capacity I ended up with, and that's still mostly the case. I'm guessing my 97 percent capacity isn't too far off from the battery health readings on iPhones that didn't have the charge limit turned on.

As for older devices, my two-year-old ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max only lost 1 percent capacity from 2025 to 2026, and my iPhone 15 Pro Max didn't lose any capacity at all during the year. Both phones had fewer battery cycles (44 and 17, respectively), but they're holding capacity even after sitting dead for short periods of time throughout the year.

The most hands-off way to manage battery health is to use Optimized Battery Charging, since it minimizes time spent at 100 percent battery while still charging to full. Setting an 80 percent limit and then turning it off on days you need 100 percent is also a good compromise that could save you battery capacity over time. Apple has 90 and 95 percent options too, which might be a better choice.

My iPhone 18 Pro Max is already set to 80 percent, so I'll check in again in September 2027. I'm going to stick with USB-C charging when I can, and I'm curious how the even bigger battery will affect longevity and what the 80 percent limit is like day to day.
What's your iPhone battery capacity and cycle count? Share it in the comments below and weigh in on whether you think battery charge limits are worthwhile.

evidence.discovery_lead: Last month, a proven leaker revealed that Apple has tested the ability to connect four HomePods to an Apple TV 4K for surround sound, with the HomePods intended to be arranged in front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right positions. Now further evidence of this functionality has surfaced ahead of an announcement from Apple. First, the same leaker known as "pdfu" has uncovered additional code related to a four-HomePod surround sound system in the latest beta of audioOS, which is Apple's internal name for the HomePod's operating system. For example, on the third audioOS 27.2 beta, he said that "Siri can match a speaker to its surround system." Second, MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris discovered that the third beta of macOS 27.2 contains two new SF Symbols depicting a group of four speakers in a room. While the HomePod is not mentioned in the names of the symbols, one of them appears to show a basic top-down view of HomePods, and the other mentions that the four speakers are part of a home theater setup. The timing of these symbols being added by Apple suggests they could be related to the rumored four-HomePod surround sound functionality. Apple plans to unveil new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K models on Tuesday, October 13 , according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, while he said that the full-sized HomePod will be updated " eventually ." However, it is unclear if this surround-sound functionality will require new HomePods. The leaker "pdfu" previously said that Apple tested two different setups, including four second-generation HomePods, and two second-generation HomePods in front positions paired with two unreleased speakers in rear positions. It is also unclear if any existing Apple TV 4K models will support four HomePods, or if the functionality will be limited to the upcoming model. Currently, you can set two HomePod or HomePod mini speakers as the default audio output on all Apple TV 4K models for stereo sound. With new HomePod and Apple TV models on the horizon, and all of the mounting evidence across Apple's software code and symbols, it seems likely that Apple will unveil this new functionality fairly soon, barring any last-minute issues. units.text: No one will admit that iPhone and Mac pricing is going to go up again, but the rest of the industry is clear that it's inevitable sooner, rather than later.
This isn't a sales post. We can't say what we're about to say any more clearly.
If you are in the market now for any Apple device at all, or you expect to be soon, do not wait. Retail pricing will not get cheaper any time soon.
Back in July 2026, Apple's attempts to keep prices steady took their first stumble. Prices of Macs and iPads went up significantly, and only really the iPhone was immune — for a brief time.

It was all very specifically because of the global chip shortage and how extraordinary demand from AI firms made it more expensive to buy processors and RAM. In August, the Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said that things would not get better until 2028.

"Even as we expect industry supply to improve gradually in 2028, we currently do not have line of sight as to when memory supply will be able to catch up with increasing demand," said Mehrotra. "AI is driving the demand, and that's where the value of memory is really high because it enables the performance of AI."

Flash forward to today when all Apple devices cost more than they did, and the company is believed to have been forced to pay double for some components. On October 1, 2026, Mehrotra was back to report that things were worse for consumers, but better for Micron from a profit standpoint.
Mehrotra says that Micron expects "memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026."
"The majority of our discussions with customers today are already around 2028," he continued in Micron's latest earnings. "Customers want assurance now even beyond [a] 2030 time frame."
Apple picked a bad time to introduce a $2,000 iPhone that is only likely to get more costly soon

He said that in an earnings call where he also reported that over 75% of Micron's 2027 output has already been sold to AI firms. It's not like consumer technology firms are likely to get the remainder, either, as Micron has been concentrating output to AI companies since in 2025, since the company makes the most money that way.
Apple has ongoing contracts with Micron, just as it does with TSMC, the firm that makes most of its processors. Neither are eternal.
For example, in July 2026, TSMC raised its prices by 10%. Apple took the hit.
Read the room

All the way back in June 2026, when he was still Apple's CEO, Tim Cook described the AI-driven chip shortages as being like a 100-year flood. "We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us," he said, "and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable."
"Unfortunately, price increases are unavoidable," said Cook. That was in June. Apple raised prices just a few days later.
Since then, everything Cook described appears to have become worse. Apple has reportedly agreed to pay $2 per gigabit of DRAM for 2027 devices, for instance, up from $1.50 per gigabit.
So the industry is saying there's no relief. In October 2026, the situation is worse and so there's no question.
Apple will raise prices again and it is only a matter of time. We're guessing there will be another product-spanning hike before the end of March.

Looking further ahead to when the AI demand falters or production capacity catches up, though, there is a further issue. No business ever lowers prices unless it believes it has to, so there is a very strong chance that prices are going to stay high forever.
Which means that Apple's current prices, as inflated as they have been, may not be coming back down. They will, instead, be going up.

Consequently, if you need any Apple devices, the time to buy is as soon as you possibly can. It's tempting to wait, especially when there are always new Apple devices expected, but this is a time for practicality.
If you need a Mac, an iPhone, or an iPad, and the currently shipping models will do what you want, don't wait.

Back in July 2026, Apple's attempts to keep prices steady took their first stumble. Prices of Macs and iPads went up significantly, and only really the iPhone was immune — for a brief time.

It was all very specifically because of the global chip shortage and how extraordinary demand from AI firms made it more expensive to buy processors and RAM. In August, the Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said that things would not get better until 2028.

"Even as we expect industry supply to improve gradually in 2028, we currently do not have line of sight as to when memory supply will be able to catch up with increasing demand," said Mehrotra. "AI is driving the demand, and that's where the value of memory is really high because it enables the performance of AI."

Flash forward to today when all Apple devices cost more than they did, and the company is believed to have been forced to pay double for some components. On October 1, 2026, Mehrotra was back to report that things were worse for consumers, but better for Micron from a profit standpoint.
Mehrotra says that Micron expects "memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026."
"The majority of our discussions with customers today are already around 2028," he continued in Micron's latest earnings. "Customers want assurance now even beyond [a] 2030 time frame."
Apple picked a bad time to introduce a $2,000 iPhone that is only likely to get more costly soon

He said that in an earnings call where he also reported that over 75% of Micron's 2027 output has already been sold to AI firms. It's not like consumer technology firms are likely to get the remainder, either, as Micron has been concentrating output to AI companies since in 2025, since the company makes the most money that way.
For example, in July 2026, TSMC raised its prices by 10%. Apple took the hit.

All the way back in June 2026, when he was still Apple's CEO, Tim Cook described the AI-driven chip shortages as being like a 100-year flood. "We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us," he said, "and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable."
Since then, everything Cook described appears to have become worse. Apple has reportedly agreed to pay $2 per gigabit of DRAM for 2027 devices, for instance, up from $1.50 per gigabit.

Consequently, if you need any Apple devices, the time to buy is as soon as you possibly can. It's tempting to wait, especially when there are always new Apple devices expected, but this is a time for practicality.

units.text: After suffering years of frustration with Apple’s parental control features, I’ve been eagerly anticipating the revamped Screen Time that launched last month with iOS 27. Unfortunately, I can’t use it.

Technically, this is because my 18-year-old son hasn’t got round to updating his MacBook. But mostly, it’s because Apple’s rollout of the new feature has been confusing and frustrating, with fiddly requirements that might have you digging through drawers for your old devices.
"“We’re working to resolve delays some families are seeing.”" - Katie Lowry, Apple spokesperson

I’m not even trying to use Screen Time on my son’s devices. He’s 18, away at college, and well beyond my parental controls. The problem is I apparently need him to update his MacBook Neo before I can use Apple’s new Screen Time features on my 15-year-old daughter’s iPhone. His college is four hours away, and like many college kids, he’s an expert at ignoring text messages from his mom asking him to do a boring chore.

My problem stems from Apple’s requirement that, to use the new Screen Time on any device in your connected household, every iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Mac, and even Vision Pro in your Apple Family Sharing group has to be updated to the relevant OS 27.

On top of that, if you have older devices that aren’t compatible with the latest OS, you can’t use the new Screen Time on them at all. While Apple says these “legacy devices” won’t prevent you from using the new Screen Time on newer devices, some users are finding they can only turn on the new Screen Time features after deleting the old gadgets from their accounts.

All of this is creating a lot of frustration for parents like me, who just want a reliable, easy way to manage their child’s screen time. I reached out to Apple about the problems I’ve been having, and the company acknowledged the issues, saying it is making changes to “resolve” them.

”This is our biggest child safety update yet, designed to give families even more tools to help keep children safe,” Apple spokesperson Katie Lowry told me. “We’re continuing to improve the rollout of the new parental controls so parents can get set up quickly and easily, and we’re working to resolve delays some families are seeing.”

[Image: Apple announced the revamped Screen Time earlier this year. Among underlying improvements and several updates, it includes new features such as Ask To Browse. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/Apple-Screen-Time-Ask-to-Browse-wwdc-2026-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Apple’s Screen Time is the company’s version of parental controls, and it’s been beset by issues since its introduction in 2018. In the years I’ve been using it, I’ve faced ongoing problems, from settings not syncing reliably across devices to trouble managing contacts and time limits remotely. And of course, my children finding ways to override my settings, thanks to Reddit threads, YouTube videos, and annoyingly good guesses.

When Apple dedicated a big slice of its 2026 WWDC keynote to Screen Time, I was hopeful it meant the company had taken parent feedback seriously and was building a more robust and easier-to-use experience. The updates and new features look promising, but I haven’t been able to try them because of the ongoing setup issues. And I’m not alone.
Alongside the roadblock with my son’s MacBook Neo (which, admittedly, is on us), I’ve run into several other hurdles while trying to access the new Screen Time.

There’s the problem that Apple thinks my Mac Mini, which I updated to macOS 27 over a week ago, is still on macOS 26. There’s the problem of my sixth-gen iPad Mini that I handed down to my son, but which Apple still lists under my name and as running iPadOS 18. Then there’s the problem that my daughter’s iPad Pro is too old to update to the latest software.
To reiterate, to use the new Screen Time on any device, every eligible device has to be updated to OS 27, because the new Screen Time uses a completely redesigned iCloud architecture.

[Image: The revamped Screen Time includes easier to use controls such as these buttons that give you quick access to common actions. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/controls__bnvrfgegztpy_large_2x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

My son’s iPad Mini is compatible, and I updated it when he was last home (without his MacBook). But when I went to enable the new Screen Time controls again, Apple showed that same iPad Mini under my account as needing to be updated. That iPad obviously doesn’t exist: a ghost iPad, you might say. Eventually, removing it from my account fixed the problem (Settings > Apple Account > Devices > Remove Device), but it took several attempts digging through menus, plus waiting a full weekend for it to clear.

In fact, all my attempts to conform to Apple’s requirements for the new Screen Time have taken a while to kick in. It seems there’s a delay between updating a device and the service becoming available. My editor updated all his devices but still didn’t have access. It was only after waiting and removing all his legacy devices — those that can’t be updated to 27 — from his account that the option appeared.

It’s unclear whether it was time or his actions that led to his eventual success. Apple’s documentation says legacy devices shouldn’t stop you from using the new Screen Time on compatible devices, but some Reddit users also found that removing them unlocked access. Either way, Apple needs to make this whole process clearer so families don’t give up on trying to access what I hope are valuable features.

[Image: These are some of the legacy devices still connected to my iCloud. I was able to remove most of them in my Apple account settings, although some refuse to leave. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/legacy-devices.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

The fact that these legacy devices can’t use the new Screen Time features raises a bigger issue. Passing older devices down to children is common in families, and the requirement to be on version 27 will mean many kids’ devices won’t get access to the improved parental controls.

For example, my daughter’s third-gen iPad Pro (a hand-me-down from my husband) taps out at iPadOS 26, meaning it can’t ever run the new Screen Time. So, she will have one device (her iPhone 15) that can use the new Screen Time and one device (her iPad) that can’t. I won’t know how this will work until I have access, but my guess is it won’t be fun.

My guess is that I’ll have to use the old Screen Time directly on the iPad, rather than managing it from my phone as I do now. This is because it won’t be compatible with the upgraded iCloud architecture that syncs settings between devices in your family group. If you have multiple older devices, you may want to just stick with the old Screen Time controls for now.

In the meantime, I’m still trying to figure out what bug is causing my Mac Mini to block the update, while continuing to nag my son to update his MacBook Neo. College is a fun, busy time, and “update software on my computer” is low on his to-do list. But his reticence just might stem from being slightly suspicious of my request to update his device so I can use Screen Time on his sister’s iPhone.

Technology certainly has added another tricky layer to the parent-child relationship. After a decade of attempting to balance giving my kids access to the benefits of technology with keeping them safe and teaching them healthy habits, I’m frankly exhausted. I have a couple of years left in my struggle, but the irony of this situation isn’t lost on me; that the system meant to protect one child now depends on the goodwill of the other, who is totally over it.

units.text: Apple is collaborating with LG on a new lineup of smart home devices, including a video doorbell, thermostat, indoor camera, and more, according to a report from Bloomberg. The products will reportedly feature LG branding but integrate with the company’s rumored smart home hub that’s expected to launch during an event on October 13th.
Sources tell Bloomberg that the upcoming line of devices also includes a deadbolt lock, outdoor security camera, and a floodlight camera.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/image-26-1.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/image-27.png?quality=90&strip=all]

Several of the devices will reportedly come with support for the smart home protocols Thread and Matter amid a “formal reboot” for Apple’s HomeKit platform. The door lock also comes with an ultra-wideband feature that could allow it to automatically unlock when a user gets near their door, according to Bloomberg.
[Image: An “LG Smart Deadbolt Lock” listed in the FCC’s database. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/image-28.png?quality=90&strip=all]

For months, rumors have suggested that Apple is planning to dive deeper into the smart home space. The company is working on a Siri AI-enabled smart home hub that comes with a six-inch display that users can mount to their wall or place on a table, Bloomberg has reported. Apple is expected to take the wraps off the upcoming device later this month, where it may also reveal a new HomePod mini and an upgraded Apple TV device.

units.text: One day after rolling out macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, Apple is now rolling out the equivalent build for users enrolled in the public beta program. Here’s what’s new.
macOS 27.2 public beta 2 now available
After a two-week hiatus, Apple released macOS 27.2 beta 3 for developers yesterday, continuing its round of testing ahead of the system’s official release in the coming weeks.

While the iOS 27.2 betas have introduced a few new features, including a redesigned Health app, dual-capture mode for Group FaceTime sessions, and Apple TV profiles in the TV app, macOS 27.2 has been less eventful, with its headline feature being the addition of five new languages to Siri AI.

As the company announced during last month’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo event, Siri AI will soon expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, joining English as a supported language.
The release build for macOS 27.2 public beta 2 is 26B5101f, which is the same as yesterday’s build.
If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.
Did you spot anything new in today’s public beta? Let us know in the comments.

evidence.discovery_lead: Microsoft is set to drop OneDrive support for iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, which will remove the cloud storage app's compatibility with several older iPhones and one iPad model. The loss of support for iOS 18 will impact the iPhone XR, iPhone XS, and iPhone XS Max, because these devices can't be updated to iOS 26. Likewise, the seventh-generation iPad will be left behind when Microsoft raises the app's minimum requirement to iPadOS 26. OneDrive 18.12.1 is the final version to support iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, based on release notes for Microsoft's latest TestFlight beta. It's not clear when the change will translate to the public version of OneDrive. That said, Microsoft recently added a notice to its App Store listing saying that support for iOS and iPadOS 18 will be dropped "soon," and recommending that users update to iOS 26 or iOS 27 to continue receiving the latest versions. Existing versions of OneDrive aren't expected to immediately stop working on affected devices, but they won't receive new features, fixes, or other app updates once Microsoft makes the change. units.text: 苹果正在测试的iOS 27.2预计将带来一项针对“信息”应用的细化控制功能，允许用户单独关闭某些由Apple Intelligence生成的“建议操作”。相比此前只能整体接受这类AI功能，这一变化将让用户能够更加精确地决定哪些建议应该出现在对话界面中。
“信息建议操作”最初出现在iOS 27测试版中，但苹果在正式发布iOS 27时暂时移除了这一功能，并表示需要更多时间进行测试。随着iOS 27.2测试版的推出，这项功能重新出现，同时苹果还进一步增加了针对不同建议类型的独立控制选项。
这项功能的主要作用，是利用Apple Intelligence理解用户正在进行的对话，并根据上下文自动提供可以一键执行的操作。例如，当对方在信息中要求用户发送一张照片时，系统可以直接显示添加相关照片的建议；如果对方邀请用户参加某个活动，系统则可以建议将活动添加到“日历”；如果对话涉及需要购买或完成的事项，系统还可以建议将内容加入“提醒事项”或“备忘录”。
苹果在iOS 27中已经将这类AI能力作为“信息”应用的重要功能之一。不过，对于一些用户而言，系统自动出现的建议按钮可能并不总是有用，甚至可能干扰正常的消息界面。因此，iOS 27.2似乎正在提供更加细致的控制方式。
根据iOS 27.2第三个测试版中的相关代码，苹果新增了一个专门用于管理“建议操作”的设置页面。目前发现的选项包括“添加到日历”、“添加到提醒事项”、“添加到备忘录”、“在地图中显示”以及“航班和包裹”等不同类型。
这意味着用户未来可以根据自己的使用习惯，逐项决定是否允许这些建议出现在“信息”应用中。例如，如果用户从来不会通过信息内容创建日历事件，就可以直接关闭“添加到日历”，而继续保留其他类型的建议。
iOS 27.2还可能提供一个名为“隐藏未使用的建议”的选项。启用之后，如果某一种建议连续30天没有被用户使用，系统就会自动停止显示这种建议。
这一机制实际上类似于一种“自适应清理”。用户不需要逐项研究所有设置，只需要正常使用信息应用，系统就会根据实际使用情况逐渐减少那些长期没有被采用的建议，从而避免界面中出现大量用户并不需要的AI操作按钮。
如果某项建议后来重新变得有用，用户也可以重新打开对应的独立开关。相关测试代码显示，关闭后再重新开启某个建议，就可以恢复其在信息应用中的显示。
从整体设计来看，苹果显然希望在AI自动化与用户控制之间寻找平衡。Apple Intelligence可以根据对话内容主动判断用户可能需要什么，但苹果并没有完全让AI决定界面中应该出现哪些操作，而是进一步提供了更加细粒度的手动控制。
这也是iOS 27中Apple Intelligence逐渐深入系统后的一个明显趋势。与单纯回答问题的聊天机器人不同，苹果的AI越来越多地承担“理解上下文并直接执行操作”的角色。信息、邮件、电话等系统应用都开始利用用户正在处理的内容，主动提供下一步操作。
目前iOS 27.2仍处于测试阶段，上述设置最终是否会以完全相同的形式出现在正式版本中仍存在变化的可能。不过，苹果已经确认“信息建议”属于iOS 27系列中的Apple Intelligence功能，并正在逐步完善相关体验。
除了信息应用的建议操作之外，iOS 27.2还包含重新设计的“健康”应用、新增的Siri AI语言以及其他功能调整。苹果此前已经宣布，Siri AI将在iOS 27.2中增加法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语支持。
目前苹果已经发布iOS 27.2测试版，而且这次更新的发布时间安排比较特殊。苹果没有先推出iOS 27.1测试版，而是直接开始测试iOS 27.2。由于首款折叠iPhone将于10月23日上市，并预装iOS 27.1，苹果预计会先针对这款新设备发布iOS 27.1，而iOS 27.2则可能在之后面向更广泛的用户推出。
如果最终保持目前的设计，iOS 27.2中的这项变化虽然并不属于大型新功能，却能够明显改善Apple Intelligence的日常使用体验。相比让AI不断向用户推送各种看似智能的操作建议，让用户决定哪些建议真正有价值，也许更符合苹果一贯强调的系统可控性和简洁性。

units.text: Apple has confirmed it will be releasing its financials for the fourth quarter of 2026 on November 2. It will mark the first results helmed by new CEO John Ternus after becoming the new head of the company.

As per regulatory rules in the United States, Apple issues a quarterly report revealing its financial performance during the period, The fourth-quarter results arrive at the start of November, as per the usual timings.
In a notification to investors and analysts, Apple has said it will be bringing out those Q4 results on November 2. The results will then be followed by the usual conference call at 5 p.m. EDT.
While CFO Kevan Parekh will be in attendance, so will new CEO John Ternus, appearing in his first as chief following the transition from Tim Cook.
As ever, AppleInsider will be analyzing the results as they are released, along with the questions and answers from the conference call.
Apple's Q4 expectations from Q3

During its Q3 2026 results, Apple provided its fourth-quarter revenue expectations. While analysts projected 12.1% growth for Q4 at the time of the guidance, Apple said it expected 9% to 11% year-over-year growth.
Revenue from iPhone is expected to go up by a mid-teens percentage, while Services should grow by a similar amount to Q3.
Apple quarterly revenue and gross margin, as of Q4 2025.
Then-CEO Tim Cook also shared that there could be problems supplying iPhones to consumers. Demand was so high that the supply chain wouldn't be able to keep up with it.
Furthermore, there was also a worry that currency changes could impact revenue growth for the period. And, of course, any memory crisis shenanigans too.
Product Changes

The fourth quarter is always a major one for Apple when it comes to product launches. However, due to the major introductions happening near the start of September, the announced items will only have a few weeks to impact Apple's bottom line.

units.text: MacRumors reports that in addition to Apple’s expected event on October 13, the company is planning to unveil another batch of new products in the final week of the month. Here are the details.
New Macs and OLED iPad mini expected before year’s end

Over the weekend, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed that Apple will, in fact, hold an event on October 13 to announce “its long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV.”

Gurman’s report came amid uncertainty over whether Apple would hold an event or announce the new products through videos and press releases, as it has done in the past. Gurman had previously said only that Apple would unveil these products on October 13, without specifying how they would be announced.

In addition to these three products, Apple had also been expected to unveil a new OLED iPad mini and new Macs, including an updated iMac and a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro, both powered by an M6 chip.
Now, MacRumors says that, “according to multiple sources familiar with the matter,” the company will unveil another round of new products in the final week of October.

The report stops short of saying which products will be announced. It also does not provide a specific date, or say whether Apple will hold a second event or unveil the products through videos and press releases.

That said, these announcements at the end of the month would cap off an unusually busy October for Apple, with the iPhone Duo launching on October 23 and the company also expected to report its quarterly results before the month is out.

units.text: In addition to releasing macOS 27.2 Golden Gate public beta 2, Apple is now rolling out the first Release Candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2. Here are the details.
Security updates continue for older macOS versions

As is usually the case for point updates of older macOS versions, Apple today rolled out the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, without first releasing regular beta versions.
Apple released macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 late last month, both of which saw two RCs before the official rollout.

Apple’s release notes for the first macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 RCs mention only that they “provide[s] important security fixes and [are] recommended for all users.” Last month’s updates contained a single CoreGraphics security fix, with its details reading:

Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.

Apple will likely detail the fixes included in macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 after their official release, which will likely come alongside macOS 27.2 Golden Gate within the next few weeks.
The release build for macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 RC 1 is 24H219, while the release build for macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 RC 1 is 25G320.
Did you spot anything new or different in today’s RCs? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: Apple is launching new products next week, with Apple TV 4K and HomePod models rumored to be among them. And leaks in the latest Apple software reveal several new Apple TV and HomePod features expected to be unveiled.
New Apple TV and HomePod features leaked in code are expected to be announced next week
Next week, Apple will unveil a fresh push into Home products, with new Apple TV 4K, ‘HomePad,’ and HomePod mini models set to launch.
We’ve already gotten plenty of leaks around new features to expect, but yesterday’s beta 3 releases of tvOS 27.2, HomePod 27.2, and iOS 27.2 reveal even more.
Aaron Perris found references in tvOS 27.2 beta 3 to Apple Intelligence coming to Apple TV. Headlined by Siri AI, these AI features are expected to be exclusive to new hardware.
He also found code in iOS 27.2 that suggests nearby home accessories could show controls in your iPhone’s Dynamic Island.

iOS 27.2 beta 3 includes new HomeKit code suggesting nearby smart-home accessories could show controls in the Dynamic Island. A new method explicitly references showing Dynamic Island controls through HomeKit’s proximity manager. This is an AI mockup of what it may look like: pic.twitter.com/szddeb2nCg
— Aaron (@aaronp613) October 6, 2026
View all comments
On the HomePod side, pdfu posted several discoveries related to the surround sound feature he previously detailed. A couple include:
Highlights from audioOS 27.2 beta 3:
Siri can match a speaker to its surround system. Code includes the diagnostic “Accessory [X] is a speaker in surround system [Y].” Relies on HomeKit exposing the surroundSystem interface.​

When HomePod is part of a Home Theater group for an eligible Apple TV, it can now use a new proxy-activation path to pass Siri requests to Apple TV. A separate, older path still forwards microphone audio to Apple TV.

The leaker also found evidence of Apple TV profiles expanding its available image options by adding characters from Apple TV shows and movies. So in addition to choosing from emoji for your profile, you’ll likely be able to make Ted Lasso, Mark S. from Severance, or Carol from Pluribus your profile image.

You’ll soon be able to choose characters from the Apple TV catalog as profile pictures for local Apple TV profiles. “Choose a character from Apple TV or an emoji.” The server endpoint continues to serve only emojis, as in previous releases. pic.twitter.com/UF4yKb95o3
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 5, 2026
In case you missed it, Apple TV profiles are expanding to iPhone and iPad for the first time in iOS and iPadOS 27.2. Until now they’ve been exclusive to tvOS.
Are you interested in Apple’s new Home products? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: A struggling English choir sets the stage for James Corden and Ruth Jones to play estranged siblings in a new Apple TV dramady.
On Tuesday, Apple TV announced "The Choir," a comedic drama created by and starring James Corden and Ruth Jones. It's the duo's first project together since "Gaven & Stacey: The Finale"

After years abroad, Ben (Corden) reluctantly returns to the English hometown he never liked and the family he left behind. A struggling local choir offers an unexpected chance to reconnect with his estranged sister, Lisa (Jones).

The ensemble cast includes Farrah Abbassy, Susan Brown, Tom Davis, Tom Edden, Jo Foster, David Harewood, Evie Jones, Gary Lamont, Stephen Leask, Emily Lloyd-Saini, Alexandria Riley, Luiis Rouf, Rosie Sheehy, Sylvestra Le Touzel, and Jason Watkins.
Jim Broadbent, James McAvoy, and Hannah Waddingham will also appear in guest roles.
The eight-episode series is currently in production. It is set to premiere globally on Apple TV in 2027. Corden previously hosted Carpool Karaoke for Apple.

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技10月7日消息，今年的iPhone 18 Pro系列主打配色是勃艮第酒红色，取代了上代的星宇橙，该配色一经上市便引发关注。 然而部分用户在社交平台上反馈，iPhone 18 Pro出现了褪色问题，涉及版本包括勃艮第酒红色和黑色，其中勃艮第酒红色版本较为明显。 根据网友晒出的图片，勃艮第酒红色iPhone 18 Pro镜头附近的颜色变得更浅，黑色版本也存在类似情况，目前苹果尚未对此作出回应。有网友建议，在户外使用时可以佩戴保护壳，以减少机身直接暴露在光照中的机会。 值得一提的是，上代产品iPhone 17 Pro系列也出现过褪色问题。当时受影响的主要是星宇橙配色，原本的橙色逐步变成了粉色。相关案例集中在特定批次，并非全量机型。受影响用户表示，日常使用过程中佩戴了保护壳，也没有使用酒精等化学清洁剂擦拭机身。 业内指出，iPhone 17 Pro改用了航空铝合金，并依靠阳极氧化工艺上色。阳极氧化膜存在微孔，生产时需要经过封孔处理来锁住染料。 褪色的根源在于，部分产品的封孔工序不到位，导致微孔未完全封闭。人体油脂和汗液渗入氧化膜内部后，会破坏染料结构，最终引发变色。 这一代iPhone 18 Pro依然延续了上代的铝合金加玻璃材质设计，褪色可能跟上色工艺有关。目前受影响的用户还是少数，相关问题可能集中在个别批次，后续情况仍有待观察。

值得一提的是，上代产品iPhone 17 Pro系列也出现过褪色问题。当时受影响的主要是星宇橙配色，原本的橙色逐步变成了粉色。相关案例集中在特定批次，并非全量机型。受影响用户表示，日常使用过程中佩戴了保护壳，也没有使用酒精等化学清洁剂擦拭机身。
业内指出，iPhone 17 Pro改用了航空铝合金，并依靠阳极氧化工艺上色。阳极氧化膜存在微孔，生产时需要经过封孔处理来锁住染料。
褪色的根源在于，部分产品的封孔工序不到位，导致微孔未完全封闭。人体油脂和汗液渗入氧化膜内部后，会破坏染料结构，最终引发变色。
这一代iPhone 18 Pro依然延续了上代的铝合金加玻璃材质设计，褪色可能跟上色工艺有关。目前受影响的用户还是少数，相关问题可能集中在个别批次，后续情况仍有待观察。

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple initially planned to equip the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iPhone Duo with 16GB of RAM, according to the leaker known as " Instant Digital ." The brief Weibo post does not say when Apple considered that capacity. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max feature 12GB of RAM, as confirmed through Xcode 27 , matching the iPhone 17 Pro models. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ is also expected to have 12GB, but the Xcode data used to verify the Pro models did not yet include the foldable. Rumors had pointed to 12GB for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ well before launch. In April 2025, supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicted that the iPhone 18 lineup would have 12GB of RAM. Analyst Jeff Pu projected the same capacity for the Pro models and Apple's first foldable iPhone in January. A March report from The Bell said Samsung would supply 12GB memory modules for the ‌iPhone Duo‌. The global memory shortage is the likely explanation for the apparent change. The March report described sharply rising prices for the 12GB modules, while Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman reported that memory costs led Apple to discuss a higher starting price for the foldable. Kuo also said DRAM shortages were forcing Apple to scale back its 2026 hardware shipment plans. ‌iPhone Duo‌ pre-orders begin October 16 , ahead of availability on October 23.
